## What this document does

All participants answered the ten final-test questions (five Polio, five TB). Each answer
is scored as the points earned out of the question's maximum (1–4 points). Because the
questions are worth different numbers of points, each question's score is modelled as
points out of its maximum with a **beta-binomial** model: a binomial model for the points
earned, with an overdispersion parameter, because a student tends to know all or none of
a question's elements. The estimates are on the probability of earning a point (μ), that
is, the expected **proportion of a question's points**, averaged over the sample.

Two sets of models:

- **Status models (pooled).** Each question is coded by its status for the participant:
  **Prequestioned** (the topic of the participant's prequestions), **Non-prequestioned**
  (the other topic, for participants given prequestions), or **no-prequestion** (participants
  without prequestions). Prequestioned − no-prequestion is the specific benefit and
  Non-prequestioned − no-prequestion the general benefit. Status + Topic.
- **Group × Topic models** (preregistered, as are the specific and general benefits): Group (Polio, TB, no-prequestion) × Topic
  (Polio, TB questions). Reported: the Polio − TB difference within each group (which
  combines any prequestion effect with differences between the Polio and TB questions) and
  the interaction contrast, the Polio group's Polio − TB difference minus the TB group's
  (in which the question differences cancel). Their Bayes factors are computed on the
  response scale (proportion of points), the scale of the estimates.

*Naming:* the paper calls the group without prequestions the **no-prequestion** condition;
in the data and code it is labelled `Control`.

Random effects: the maximal structure warranted by the design, by-participant intercepts
and Topic slopes and by-question intercepts and Status (or Group) slopes (every question was
answered in all three statuses and by all three groups). Status, Group and Topic have equal-prior contrasts
(`bayestestR::contr.equalprior_pairs`), so every pairwise difference has the same
normal(0, 1.5) prior on the log-odds scale. Bayes factors are Savage–Dickey
(`bayestestR::bayesfactor_parameters()`) on the link-scale comparisons from `modelbased`,
against draws from the same model sampled from its priors. Shared code is in
`R/bayes_helpers.R`; fits are cached in `analysis/brms_cache/`.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
fit_settings <- list(chains = 4, iter = 11000, warmup = 1000, adapt_delta = 0.95, refit = FALSE)
if (exists("params")) {
  fit_settings <- modifyList(fit_settings, params[intersect(names(params), names(fit_settings))])
}
source(here("R", "setup.R"))
source(here("R", "data.R"))
source(here("R", "bayes_helpers.R"))
```

## Data

```{r}
#| label: data
# One row per participant x question (grade_test.R), analysed participants
test_items <- read_csv(here("data", "derived", "test_scored_items.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(et_id %in% levels(dat$participant)) |>
  transmute(participant = factor(et_id),
            condition = factor(recode(et_group, Po = "Polio"), levels = c("Control", "Polio", "TB")),
            topic = factor(topic, levels = c("Polio", "TB")),
            question = factor(questnum), points, max_points) |>
  mutate(status = case_when(condition == "Control" ~ "Control",
                            as.character(topic) == as.character(condition) ~ "Prequestioned",
                            TRUE ~ "Non-prequestioned"),
         status = factor(status, levels = c("Prequestioned", "Non-prequestioned", "Control"))) |>
  equal_prior()
test_items_cond <- cond_coding(test_items)

test_items |>
  group_by(status, topic) |>
  summarise(n = n(), prop_points = sum(points) / sum(max_points), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Observed proportion of points by status and topic")
```

## Models

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| results: hide
m_test  <- list(final_test = fit_betabin("status + topic", "bayes_status_final_test_bb", test_items))
m_topic <- list(final_test = fit_betabin("condition * topic", "bayes_cond_topic_final_test_bb",
                                         test_items_cond, re = re_test_cond))
```

```{r}
#| label: diagnostics
diag_tab <- bind_rows(diag_model(m_test$final_test, "final_test"),
                      diag_model(m_topic$final_test, "final_test (Group × Topic)"))
diag_tab
```

### Choice of model: posterior predictive checks

Questions are worth 1–4 points, so a score can only take a few values (0, .25, .33, .5,
.67, .75, 1). The beta-binomial is compared with a binomial model (no overdispersion), with the same
predictors and random effects, by how well each reproduces how often each score occurred.

```{r}
#| label: model-choice
#| results: hide
m_bin <- fit_brm(as.formula(paste("points | trials(max_points) ~ status + topic +", re_test)),
                 test_items, binomial(),
                 c(prior_string(sprintf("normal(0, %s)", s_logit), class = "b"),
                   prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "Intercept"), prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sd"),
                   prior(lkj(2), class = "cor")),
                 "bayes_status_final_test_binomial")
```

```{r}
#| label: model-choice-table
set.seed(2026)
nd <- 1000
obs_prop <- test_items$points / test_items$max_points
max_mat <- matrix(test_items$max_points, nd, nrow(test_items), byrow = TRUE)
yrep <- list(`Beta-binomial` = posterior_predict(m_test$final_test, ndraws = nd) / max_mat,
             Binomial = posterior_predict(m_bin, ndraws = nd) / max_mat)
score_fit <- imap(yrep, \(y, nm) score_freq(y, obs_prop) |> mutate(model = nm)) |> bind_rows()
score_fit |>
  select(score, observed, model, predicted) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = predicted) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Share of responses at each score: observed and predicted (posterior mean)")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
ppc_scores(m_test$final_test, "Status model") + ppc_scores(m_topic$final_test, "Group × Topic model")
```

## Status models: prequestioned and non-prequestioned vs. no-prequestion

```{r}
#| label: status
bf_tab <- bf_table(m_test)
est_tab <- contrasts_by(m_test)
means_tab <- means_by(m_test, "status")
means_draws <- mean_draws_by(m_test, "status")
bf_tab |> transmute(comparison, BF10, BF01) |> kable(digits = 2)
est_tab
means_tab
```

## Group × Topic

```{r}
#| label: group-topic
# proportion of points: Bayes factors on the response scale, the scale of the estimates
bf_topic_tab <- bf_table(m_topic, topic_draws, response_scale = "final_test")
est_topic_tab <- topic_estimates(m_topic)
means_topic_tab <- means_by(m_topic, c("condition", "topic")) |> add_status()
means_topic_draws <- mean_draws_by(m_topic, c("condition", "topic")) |> add_status()
bf_topic_tab |> transmute(comparison, BF10, BF01) |> kable(digits = 2)
est_topic_tab
means_topic_tab
```

## Prior sensitivity

```{r}
#| label: priorsense
sens_tab <- sens_table(c(m_test, set_names(m_topic, "final_test (Group × Topic)")))
sens_tab
```

## Results file

```{r}
#| label: save-results
save_results(list(diag = diag_tab, bf = bf_tab, est = est_tab, means = means_tab,
                  means_draws = means_draws, bf_topic = bf_topic_tab, est_topic = est_topic_tab,
                  means_topic = means_topic_tab, means_topic_draws = means_topic_draws,
                  score_fit = score_fit,
                  sens = sens_tab),
             here("analysis", "results_final_test.rds"))
```
